This method can only be called once and cannot be called after
`Future.set_result()` or `Future.set_exception()` have been
called.

set_result(result)¶

Sets the result of the work associated with the `Future` to
result.

This method should only be used by `Executor` implementations and
unit tests.

Changed in version 3.8: This method raises
`concurrent.futures.InvalidStateError` if the `Future` is
already done.

set_exception(exception)¶

Sets the result of the work associated with the `Future` to the
`Exception` exception.

This method should only be used by `Executor` implementations and
unit tests.

Changed in version 3.8: This method raises
`concurrent.futures.InvalidStateError` if the `Future` is
already done.

Module Functions¶
concurrent.futures.wait(fs, timeout=None, return_when=ALL_COMPLETED)¶

timeout can be used to control the maximum number of seconds to wait before
returning. timeout can be an int or float. If timeout is not specified
or `None`, there is no limit to the wait time.

return_when indicates when this function should return. It must be one of
the following constants:

Constant

Description

concurrent.futures.FIRST_COMPLETED¶

The function will return when any future finishes or is cancelled.

concurrent.futures.FIRST_EXCEPTION¶

The function will return when any future finishes by raising an
exception. If no future raises an exception
then it is equivalent to `ALL_COMPLETED`.

concurrent.futures.ALL_COMPLETED¶

The function will return when all futures finish or are cancelled.

concurrent.futures.as_completed(fs, timeout=None)¶

See also

PEP 3148 – futures - execute computations asynchronously

The proposal which described this feature for inclusion in the Python
standard library.

Exception classes¶

exception concurrent.futures.TimeoutError¶

A deprecated alias of `TimeoutError`,
raised when a future operation exceeds the given timeout.

Changed in version 3.11: This class was made an alias of `TimeoutError`.

exception concurrent.futures.BrokenExecutor¶

Derived from `RuntimeError`, this exception class is raised
when an executor is broken for some reason, and cannot be used
to submit or execute new tasks.

Added in version 3.7.

skill_drafts.name: Future State Transition Control
skill_drafts.description: Set the result or exception of a Future object exactly once, enforcing state immutability. Use when an Executor or test harness needs to mark a parallel task as complete.
applicable_signals: Future object exists and is not yet done
Task execution has produced a result or raised an exception
Caller is Executor implementation or test code
contraindications: Future is already done (set_result or set_exception already called)
Caller is not an Executor implementation or unit test
Future object is None or invalid
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Check that Future is not yet done', 'detail': 'Verify Future state before attempting transition'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Call set_result(result) if task succeeded', 'detail': 'Pass the computed result value to finalize Future'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Or call set_exception(exception) if task raised', 'detail': 'Pass the Exception object to record failure'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Future transitions to done state', 'detail': 'State is now immutable; subsequent calls will raise InvalidStateError'}
triggers: Executor implementation completes a parallel task and must record outcome
Unit test harness needs to simulate task completion
Parallel task result or exception is ready to be stored
constraints: Method can only be called once per Future
Cannot be called after set_result() or set_exception() have already been called
Raises InvalidStateError if Future is already done (Python 3.8+)
cautions: This method is intended for internal use by Executor implementations and tests only
Misuse outside of Executor context may lead to state corruption
InvalidStateError indicates an attempt to transition an already-finalized Future
output_contract: Future transitions to done state with result or exception recorded. Subsequent calls to set_result() or set_exception() on the same Future raise concurrent.futures.InvalidStateError. Downstream callers can now safely call result() or exception() without blocking.

metadata.prompt: Call set_result(result) or set_exception(exception) on a Future object to atomically finalize its state. Each Future may transition to done state only once. After either method succeeds, the Future is immutable and subsequent calls will raise InvalidStateError. Use only within Executor implementations or unit tests.

skill_drafts.name: Parallel Task Completion Polling
skill_drafts.description: Wait for one or more Futures to complete with configurable timeout and return condition. Supports three completion modes: return when any task finishes (FIRST_COMPLETED), return when any task raises an exception (FIRST_EXCEPTION), or return when all tasks finish (ALL_COMPLETED). Use to synchronize on parallel task outcomes and partition results into done and pending sets.
applicable_signals: Multiple Futures submitted to ThreadPoolExecutor or ProcessPoolExecutor
Synchronization point required before inspecting or processing results
Timeout constraint or early-exit condition specified by caller
contraindications: Non-blocking polling is preferred; use as_completed() iterator instead
No timeout constraint and caller can iterate over results as they arrive
Single Future result retrieval; use Future.result() directly
workflow_steps: Prepare a collection of Future objects from submitted tasks
Determine timeout value (seconds) or None for no limit
Select return_when constant based on synchronization strategy
Iterate over done set to retrieve results or handle exceptions
If pending is non-empty, decide whether to retry, cancel, or log
triggers: Caller submits multiple tasks to an Executor and needs to block until one or more reach a terminal state
Timeout or early-exit strategy is required to avoid indefinite blocking
Caller must partition results into completed and pending sets for downstream handling
constraints: fs parameter must be a non-empty collection of Future objects
timeout must be None, int, or float; negative values are treated as zero
return_when must be one of the three module constants: FIRST_COMPLETED, FIRST_EXCEPTION, or ALL_COMPLETED
Function may raise TimeoutError if timeout is exceeded and no Futures have completed
cautions: TimeoutError is a deprecated alias of built-in TimeoutError as of Python 3.11
If a Future is cancelled before wait() returns, it appears in the done set
FIRST_EXCEPTION mode returns immediately only if an exception is raised; if no exception occurs, it waits like ALL_COMPLETED
output_contract: Returns a tuple (done, pending) where done is a set of Futures that have completed (finished, raised exception, or were cancelled) and pending is a set of Futures still running. Caller can call Future.result() or Future.exception() on items in done to retrieve outcomes. If timeout is exceeded before return condition is met, raises TimeoutError.

metadata.prompt: Call concurrent.futures.wait(fs, timeout=None, return_when=ALL_COMPLETED) with a collection of Future objects. Specify timeout in seconds (int or float) to limit wait duration; None means no limit. Choose return_when constant to control early exit: FIRST_COMPLETED returns immediately when any Future finishes or is cancelled; FIRST_EXCEPTION returns when any Future raises an exception (or behaves like ALL_COMPLETED if none raise); ALL_COMPLETED waits for all Futures to finish or be cancelled. The function returns a tuple (done, pending) where done is a set of completed Futures and pending is a set of Futures still running.

skill_drafts.name: Concurrent Futures Exception Handling
skill_drafts.description: Recognize and handle four exception types raised by concurrent.futures operations: CancelledError, TimeoutError, BrokenExecutor, and InvalidStateError. Use to implement robust error recovery in parallel task workflows.
skill_drafts.objective: classify and respond to executor/future failures
contraindications: No parallel tasks are in flight
intervention_moves: Route to appropriate recovery handler (retry, fallback, escalate, or abort)
triggers: Executor or Future operation raises an exception
Caller must decide whether to retry, escalate, or abort
constraints: Exception must originate from concurrent.futures module
Classification must occur before recovery action is selected
cautions: BrokenExecutor indicates executor is permanently broken; do not attempt to reuse the same executor instance
InvalidStateError (Python 3.8+) indicates Future is already done; do not call set_result() or set_exception() again
TimeoutError is a deprecated alias of built-in TimeoutError as of Python 3.11
output_contract: Exception is caught, classified into one of four types, and appropriate recovery action (retry, fallback, or escalation) is triggered; downstream caller receives clear signal of failure mode and recommended next step.

metadata.prompt: When an Executor or Future operation raises an exception, classify it as one of four types: (1) CancelledError—future was cancelled; (2) TimeoutError—future operation exceeded timeout; (3) BrokenExecutor—executor is broken and cannot accept new tasks; (4) InvalidStateError—Future state is invalid (e.g., set_result() called twice). For each type, trigger the appropriate recovery action: retry, fallback, or escalation.
